title: Never Appear Too Perfect
coreMove: Show enough imperfection or restraint that excellence does not harden into envy
sourcePressure: Chapter 46 centers on the risk of provoking envy by appearing too complete, flawless, or elevated above everyone else. The law's practical claim is narrower than fake humility: visible imperfection or restraint can reduce resentment and keep cooperation intact. Its limit is that one should not confuse strategic softening with surrendering real competence or trustworthiness. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
